applicabilityBasis.summary: Hubble USDH is a dollar-soft-pegged Solana token minted through collateralized borrowing. Its own FAQ expressly calls it a medium of exchange or payment for goods and services. The peg-stability module swaps USDH for USDC tokens with a redemption fee; crypto-collateral and USDC-token conversion do not by themselves establish an issuer obligation to redeem for fixed monetary value under GENIUS sections 2(17) and 2(22). The payment limb is supported, but a legally obligated cash/deposit issuer is not established, so applicability remains unclear rather than definitively non-payment.

genius.notes: The May 19, 2025 terms identify Vertex Labs INC., a Republic of Panama company, only as the site operator. Sections 1.3 and 6.3 disclaim operation/control of the Hubble Smart Contract System and responsibility for traded tokens. Do not equate this operator with the USDH issuer; issuerEntity and issuerDomicile are omitted. Public reserve disclosure means protocol collateral/vault transparency, not confirmation of GENIUS-eligible reserves or reserve sufficiency. No public issuer 1:1 cash/deposit redemption policy or monthly independent reserve attestation was located in the checked disclosures; documented collateral/token redemption mechanics still exist. The Act remains pre-effective under the October 7, 2026 regime review: the September 30 SCRC procedural interim rule is not the comprehensive final-regulation trigger. General DASP restrictions begin July 18, 2028; foreign-offer lawful-order requirements follow Act effectiveness. No approval, unlawful status, whole-protocol exemption or registered foreign exception is inferred.

negativeEvidenceReview.summary: No public GENIUS PPSI approval, state qualification, official pending application, foreign registration/comparability decision, or issuer-announced GENIUS intent naming Hubble USDH, Hubble Protocol and Vertex Labs INC. was found in the opened implementation materials, NYDFS directory, protocol/legal disclosures and exact-name regulator-domain searches. General rulemaking pages are not comprehensive issuer approval directories; this is a dated bounded negative-evidence finding, not proof that no confidential filing exists or a finding of unlawful issuance.
